# JOS MAR – ECW Clinic – 11/20/2026

### Patient Contact and Care Information
- **Patient:** JOS MAR
- **DOB:** Not Provided
- **Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh
- **Visit:** Cardiovascular screening / Family history of cardiomyopathy

### Front Desk Instructions
- **CPT 99214** – Established patient office visit.
- [ ] Schedule follow-up appointment in six months.
- [ ] Ensure previously ordered laboratory work is completed before follow-up.
- [ ] Prepare copies of the EKG and echocardiogram for the patient to hand-carry to the genetic testing team.
- [ ] Provide the genetic testing referral letter below.

### Patient Instructions – English
1. Please complete the laboratory work as ordered.
2. Bring your EKG, echocardiogram, and genetic testing referral letter with you to the genetic testing appointment.
3. Return for your six-month follow-up with Dr. Singh.

### Instrucciones para el Paciente – Español
1. Complete los análisis de laboratorio que se le ordenaron.
2. Lleve su electrocardiograma (EKG), ecocardiograma y carta de referencia a su cita con el equipo de pruebas genéticas.
3. Regrese para su cita de seguimiento con el Dr. Singh en seis meses.

---

## Telephone Encounter – Letter to Genetic Testing Team

<WritingBlock id="63821" variant="document">**Date: November 20, 2026**

**Dear Colleague,**

The family of Jose Marquez is well known to us.

His father developed cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias at 45 years of age. His brother manifested the phenotype at 20 years of age.

Although he was previously informed at the time of his brother's transplant that there was no genetic component to his brother's condition, Jose is now the third member of this family to present to me for cardiovascular screening.

His echocardiogram is normal, and a copy is attached for your review. We will also be attaching his EKG.

The laboratory work has been ordered, and the patient will bring the results and/or laboratory documentation with him by hand.

The three documents he will hand-carry are:

1. EKG
2. Echocardiogram
3. This referral letter

Please feel free to contact me to discuss the case.

**Direct telephone:** 805-89-04-2024

Sincerely,

**Karandeep Singh, MD**</WritingBlock>

# ALM CUE – ECW Clinic – 11/20/2026

### 1. Patient Contact and Care Information

- **Patient:** ALM CUE
- **DOB:** Not Provided
- **Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh
- **Encounter:** Repeat dictation – updated medication management
- **Team Flag:** Previous dictation exists above. Review both entries and reconcile medication changes to prevent duplicate or conflicting chart documentation.

### 2. Front Desk Instructions

**CPT Codes**
- 99215 – Established patient office visit.
- 93000 – Electrocardiogram.
- No G2211.

**Medication Changes / Prescriptions**

1. **Metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg**
   - Take one tablet PO twice daily.
   - Quantity: 60 tablets / 30 days.
   - Duration: 180 days.
   - Refills: 5.

2. **Amiodarone 200 mg**
   - Take one tablet PO twice daily.
   - Quantity: 60 tablets / 30 days.
   - Duration: 180 days.
   - Refills: 5.
   - Reassess in four weeks with plan to reduce to 200 mg once daily.

3. **Eliquis 2.5 mg**
   - Take one tablet PO twice daily.
   - Quantity: 60 tablets / 30 days.
   - Duration: 180 days.
   - Refills: 5.
   - Replaces warfarin. Lower dose selected because of history of falls.

**Discontinue:**
- Lisinopril.
- Warfarin.

**Additional Tasks**
- [ ] Prepare telephone encounter letter for Dr. Morgan Lyons, Magnolia Clinic.
- [ ] Schedule four-week follow-up for amiodarone reassessment.
- [ ] Provide updated medication instructions to patient.

### 3. Patient Instructions – English

1. Stop taking warfarin. Eliquis 2.5 mg twice daily is replacing warfarin. Do not take both medications together.
2. Eliquis is being prescribed at a lower dose because of your history of falls.
3. Stop lisinopril.
4. Start metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg twice daily.
5. Take amiodarone 200 mg twice daily.
6. Return in four weeks for reassessment. The plan is to reduce amiodarone to 200 mg once daily after reassessment.
7. Take the enclosed letter to Dr. Morgan Lyons at Magnolia Clinic.

### Instrucciones para el Paciente – Español

1. Suspenda la warfarina. Eliquis 2.5 mg dos veces al día reemplaza la warfarina. No tome ambos medicamentos juntos.
2. Se le está recetando una dosis más baja de Eliquis debido a sus antecedentes de caídas.
3. Suspenda el lisinopril.
4. Comience metoprolol succinato ER 25 mg dos veces al día.
5. Tome amiodarona 200 mg dos veces al día.
6. Regrese en cuatro semanas para una reevaluación. El plan es reducir la amiodarona a 200 mg una vez al día después de la reevaluación.
7. Lleve la carta adjunta a la Dra. Morgan Lyons en Magnolia Clinic.

---

## Telephone Encounter – Letter to Dr. Morgan Lyons

<WritingBlock id="73519" variant="document">**Date: November 20, 2026**

**To: Dr. Morgan Lyons**  
Magnolia Clinic

**Re: Alma Cuevas – Medication Management and Cardiovascular Follow-Up**

Dear Dr. Lyons,

I am writing regarding our mutual patient, Alma Cuevas.

Her recent EKG is not convincing for atrial flutter and is more consistent with sinus tachycardia. However, despite resting, her heart rate remains elevated at approximately 104 beats per minute. Clinically, I remain concerned about the possibility of underlying atrial flutter that may not be fully demonstrated on the current EKG.

Given the persistent tachycardia, I have made the following medication adjustments:

1. **Metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg twice daily** has been initiated for heart rate control.
2. **Amiodarone 200 mg twice daily** has been prescribed, with reassessment in four weeks and a plan to reduce it to 200 mg once daily thereafter.
3. **Lisinopril has been discontinued.**
4. **Warfarin has been discontinued and replaced with Eliquis 2.5 mg twice daily.** The lower Eliquis dose was selected in consideration of her history of falls.

I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss her clinical situation and coordinate her ongoing management with you.

Thank you very much for your assistance and continued care of our mutual patient. I would be grateful if you could kindly call me directly on my cell phone so that we may discuss her case and remain in close communication.

**My cell phone: 805-890-4204**

Thank you again for your collaboration.

Warm regards,

**Karandeep Singh, MD**</WritingBlock>

---

### 1. Patient Contact and Care Information
- **Patient:** DAN HIL

- **Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh
- **Visit:** Cardiovascular follow-up
- **Accompanied by:** Patient came alone.

### 2. Front Desk Instructions

**CPT Codes**
- 99214 – Established patient office visit.
- 93000 – ECG.
- G2211 – Longitudinal care complexity add-on.

**Medication Management**
- [ ] Reinforce amiodarone 100 mg PO Monday, Wednesday, and Friday only.
- [ ] Contact patient within 1–2 weeks, no later than the first week of December, for medication reconciliation.
- [ ] Obtain photographs of medication bottles from the patient via iPhone and review them with staff.
- [ ] Confirm discontinuation of daily amiodarone dosing and reinforce the Monday/Wednesday/Friday schedule.

**CCM / Remote Monitoring**
- [ ] Send message to Mr. Paulson to reinforce monthly CCM telephone calls.
- [ ] Arrange next CCM call within 1–2 weeks.
- [ ] Request and review screenshots of home blood pressure and heart rate readings.
- [ ] Reconcile medications during the CCM call.

**Next Visit – Six Months**
- [ ] Schedule cardiology follow-up in six months.
- [ ] Arrange diabetic laboratory testing 3–7 days before the appointment, including:
  - CBC
  - CMP
  - Hemoglobin A1c
  - Lipid panel
  - TSH
  - Free T4
- [ ] Associate TSH and free T4 testing with hypothyroidism (E03.9).

### 3. Patient Instructions – English

1. Take amiodarone 100 mg only on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Do not take it daily.

3. Please provide screenshots of your home blood pressure and heart rate readings.
4. Our office will contact you within the next 1–2 weeks for medication reconciliation and a CCM follow-up call.
5. Continue your monthly telephone follow-ups with our care management team.
6. Your recent kidney function, liver function, blood counts, and laboratory results were reviewed.
7. Complete your diabetic laboratory testing 3–7 days before your next appointment in six months.

6. Se revisaron sus resultados recientes de laboratorio, incluyendo la función renal, hepática y los recuentos sanguíneos.
7. Complete sus análisis de laboratorio para diabetes entre 3 y 7 días antes de su próxima cita dentro de seis meses.

## ART HER – ECW Clinic – 11/20/2026

### 1. Patient Contact and Care Information
- **Patient:** ART HER
- **DOB:** Not Provided
- **Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh
- **Visit:** New Patient Cardiovascular Evaluation
- **Accompanied by:** Not specified.

### 2. Front Desk Instructions

**CPT Codes**
- 99204 – New patient office visit.
- 93000 – Electrocardiogram.

**Priority Orders and Scheduling**

- [ ] **Echocardiogram:** Arrange as soon as possible, preferably today or early next week, to reassess LV function and cardiomyopathy (I42.9).
- [ ] Schedule cardiology follow-up in approximately six weeks.
- [ ] Arrange comprehensive laboratory testing 3–7 days before follow-up for cardiomyopathy, hypertension, and prediabetes (I42.9, I10, R73.03). Confirm specific laboratory panel with physician.
- [ ] Arrange urinalysis and urine toxicology screening at the six-week follow-up.
- [ ] Provide patient with blood pressure monitoring log from the front desk.
- [ ] Instruct patient to record blood pressure every morning and bring the completed log to follow-up.
- [ ] Request that patient bring all current medication bottles to the next appointment.
- [ ] Reconcile medication list and remove obsolete antibiotics and medications that patient is no longer taking.
- [ ] Review echocardiogram findings to determine whether ICD or pacemaker evaluation is necessary.

**Medication Review**
- Continue Entresto twice daily as prescribed.
- Continue metoprolol pending reassessment.
- Continue allopurinol for gout.
- Patient reports temporary use of ibuprofen and Norco for recent elbow fracture.
- Consider transition from metoprolol to carvedilol because of persistent hypertension and cardiomyopathy; pending physician decision.

### 3. Patient Instructions – English

1. Take Entresto twice daily as prescribed. Do not take it only once daily.
2. Continue your metoprolol and allopurinol as prescribed.
3. Stop alcohol completely. Avoid methamphetamine and other recreational drugs.
4. Check your blood pressure every morning. Record the readings on the blood pressure log provided by our office.
5. Bring your completed blood pressure log and all medication bottles to your next appointment.
6. Complete your blood work 3–7 days before your six-week follow-up.
7. An echocardiogram will be arranged as soon as possible to evaluate your heart function.
8. Urine testing, including toxicology screening, will be performed at your follow-up.
9. Keep all scheduled appointments. Regular follow-up is particularly important for monitoring your heart function and determining whether additional treatment, such as a pacemaker or defibrillator, may be necessary.

### Instrucciones para el Paciente – Español

1. Tome Entresto dos veces al día, según lo recetado. No lo tome solamente una vez al día.
2. Continúe tomando metoprolol y allopurinol según las indicaciones.
3. Suspenda completamente el consumo de alcohol. Evite la metanfetamina y otras drogas recreativas.
4. Revise su presión arterial todas las mañanas y anote los resultados en el registro proporcionado por nuestra oficina.
5. Traiga su registro de presión arterial y todos sus frascos de medicamentos a su próxima cita.
6. Complete sus análisis de sangre entre 3 y 7 días antes de su cita de seguimiento en seis semanas.
7. Se programará un ecocardiograma lo antes posible para evaluar la función de su corazón.
8. Se realizarán análisis de orina, incluyendo una prueba toxicológica, durante su próxima visita.
9. Es muy importante asistir a todas sus citas para vigilar la función cardíaca y determinar si necesita tratamiento adicional, como un marcapasos o desfibrilador.

### 1. Patient Contact and Care Information
- **Patient:** Name not provided in dictation.
- **Accompanied by:** Daughter, Rosie.
- **Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh.
- **Visit:** Blood pressure management and pacemaker follow-up.

### 2. Front Desk Instructions

**CPT Code**
- 99214 – Established patient office visit.
- No G2211.
- No 93000 today.

**Medication Changes**
- **Losartan:** Increase/return to 100 mg PO daily. Continue existing prescription.
- **Metoprolol succinate ER 25 mg:**
  - Take one tablet PO twice daily.
  - Quantity: 60 tablets.
  - Days supply: 30.
  - Refills: 5.
  - Duration: 180 days.
  - New prescription to be sent.

**CCM / Pacemaker Monitoring – Priority**
- [ ] Flag patient for CCM follow-up between November 27 and December 4, 2026.
- [ ] Arrange additional CCM telephone encounter approximately seven days from today, separate from the December 28 appointment.
- [ ] Review home blood pressure readings and response to medication adjustments.
- [ ] Flag patient for pacemaker monitoring team.
- [ ] Verify pacemaker remote transmissions are being received and reviewed.
- [ ] Coordinate ongoing pacemaker monitoring with the device team.

**Blood Pressure Monitoring**
- Target blood pressure: 130–150 systolic and 80–85 diastolic.
- Review for recurrent dizziness or symptomatic hypotension.

### 3. Patient Instructions – English

1. Increase losartan to 100 mg once daily.
2. Increase metoprolol succinate ER to 25 mg twice daily.
3. Continue monitoring your blood pressure at home and maintain a record of your readings.
4. Target blood pressure is approximately 130–150/80–85.
5. Our CCM team will contact you between November 27 and December 4 to review your blood pressure and medications.
6. Continue your scheduled December 28 appointment.
7. Our pacemaker monitoring team will continue coordinating your device transmissions.

### Instrucciones para el Paciente – Español

1. Aumente losartán a 100 mg una vez al día.
2. Aumente metoprolol succinato ER a 25 mg dos veces al día.
3. Continúe revisando su presión arterial en casa y mantenga un registro de sus lecturas.
4. La presión arterial deseada es aproximadamente 130–150/80–85.
5. Nuestro equipo de CCM se comunicará con usted entre el 27 de noviembre y el 4 de diciembre para revisar su presión arterial y sus medicamentos.
6. Mantenga su cita programada para el 28 de diciembre.
7. Nuestro equipo de monitoreo de marcapasos continuará coordinando la revisión de las transmisiones de su dispositivo.

- **Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh

- 93000 – Electrocardiogram.
- G2211 – Longitudinal care complexity add-on.

5. Continue participating in your scheduled monitoring and follow-up calls.
6. Return to Dr. Singh in four months.

5. Continúe participando en las llamadas de seguimiento y monitoreo programadas.
6. Regrese con el Dr. Singh en cuatro meses.

**Alprazolam 0.5 mg three times daily is my leading medication suspect** for dry mouth, although it is less clearly associated with dry eyes. The combination of **dry eyes and dry mouth** also raises concern for Sjögren syndrome.

| Medication | Dry mouth | Dry eyes |
|---|---|---|
| **Alprazolam 0.5 mg TID** | Recognized side effect | Possible |
| **Hydrocodone/acetaminophen** | Common | Less common |
| **Atenolol 12.5 mg daily** | Possible | Possible |
| **Amlodipine 10 mg** | Possible | Uncommon |
| **Dicyclomine 10 mg** *(listed as not taking)* | Very common | Can cause dry eyes |

**My clinical differential:**

1. **Medication-induced sicca symptoms**, particularly alprazolam, with possible contribution from hydrocodone and atenolol.
2. **Sjögren syndrome**, especially if both symptoms are persistent or accompanied by dental problems, dry-food swallowing difficulty, or joint symptoms.
3. Other contributors, including dehydration or diabetes.

If symptoms are persistent, consider reviewing the medication timeline and evaluating for Sjögren syndrome with anti-SSA/Ro, anti-SSB/La, ANA, and objective tear/salivary testing as appropriate.

Do not abruptly stop alprazolam.

**One important question:** Does the patient have dry eyes and dry mouth throughout the day, or do symptoms become worse after taking alprazolam or hydrocodone?

parts:
For **TER RIV (Teresa Rivers)**, the new combination of **dry eyes, dry mouth, and dry nose** suggests a generalized sicca syndrome. I would consider medication-related dryness, but I would also investigate **Sjögren disease**, particularly because multiple mucosal surfaces are involved.

Her diabetes is reportedly well controlled, and medication reconciliation does not reveal an obvious strong anticholinergic agent among the medications currently listed as taking.

## 1. Suggested laboratory evaluation

Your proposed **CRP, ANA, and rheumatoid factor** are reasonable starting tests. I would add anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La antibodies, which are particularly relevant to Sjögren evaluation.

| Test | Clinical purpose |
|---|---|
| **ANA with titer and pattern** | Autoimmune connective tissue disease screening |
| **Anti-SSA/Ro (Ro52/Ro60)** | Particularly important for Sjögren disease |
| **Anti-SSB/La** | Additional supportive autoimmune marker |
| **Rheumatoid factor** | Sjögren-associated autoimmunity and rheumatoid arthritis |
| **ESR and CRP** | Systemic inflammatory assessment |
| **CBC with differential** | Anemia, leukopenia, other hematologic abnormalities |
| **CMP** | Kidney function, calcium, liver function, electrolytes, and total protein |
| **Hemoglobin A1c** | Confirm continued glycemic control |
| **TSH and free T4** | Assess thyroid replacement and possible contributing thyroid dysfunction |

A negative antibody panel would not completely exclude Sjögren disease, particularly when the clinical symptoms are convincing.

### 2. Additional tests if initial screening is abnormal

I would consider **C3, C4, quantitative immunoglobulins (particularly IgG), serum protein electrophoresis, and urinalysis with urine protein assessment** if suspicion remains high or initial results suggest systemic involvement.

Anti-CCP can be useful if she has inflammatory joint symptoms. Anti-TPO antibodies may be reasonable if autoimmune thyroid disease is suspected.

For persistent symptoms, an ophthalmology assessment with **Schirmer testing and ocular surface staining**, along with salivary flow measurement, may be more informative than adding increasingly broad antibody panels. In selected seronegative cases, a minor salivary gland biopsy may be appropriate. <Cite refs={["turn856364search0","turn856364search3","turn856364search38"]}/>

### 3. Medication review: an important finding

**Timolol ophthalmic 0.5% twice daily** deserves particular attention. Although given as eye drops, timolol can be systemically absorbed. Its prescribing information identifies both dry eyes and dry mouth as possible adverse reactions. <Cite ref="turn612523search0"/>

I would specifically establish whether her dryness began after initiating or changing the timolol. Coordinate any substitution with her ophthalmologist, particularly if she uses it for glaucoma. Do not discontinue it without an alternative plan.

Her **levothyroxine** also makes thyroid function worth confirming. The other listed medications do not immediately suggest a major anticholinergic burden.

### 4. Sugar-free lozenges suitable for diabetes

I would favor xylitol-based sugar-free products intended specifically for xerostomia.

## 1\. Suggested laboratory evaluation

Your proposed **CRP, ANA, and rheumatoid factor** are reasonable starting tests. I would add anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La antibodies, which are particularly relevant to Sjögren evaluation.

| Test | Clinical purpose |
|--------|--------|
| **ANA with titer and pattern** | Autoimmune connective tissue disease screening |
| **Anti-SSA/Ro (Ro52/Ro60)** | Particularly important for Sjögren disease |
| **Anti-SSB/La** | Additional supportive autoimmune marker |
| **Rheumatoid factor** | Sjögren-associated autoimmunity and rheumatoid arthritis |
| **ESR and CRP** | Systemic inflammatory assessment |
| **CBC with differential** | Anemia, leukopenia, other hematologic abnormalities |
| **CMP** | Kidney function, calcium, liver function, electrolytes, and total protein |

I would consider **C3, C4, quantitative immunoglobulins (particularly IgG), serum protein electrophoresis, and urinalysis with urine protein assessment** if suspicion remains high or initial results suggest systemic involvement.

For **TER RIV (Teresa Rivers)**, with dry eyes, dry mouth, and dry nose, I would recommend a **saline-based nasal moisturizer**, preferably a gel rather than just a spray if the dryness is persistent.

## Nasal dryness – Recommended options

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Ayr Saline Nasal Gel original tube product" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="112px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity category="product" value="Ayr Saline Nasal Gel"/>**

      My first choice. Apply a small amount just inside each nostril with a clean fingertip or cotton swab, typically 2–3 times daily as needed. Particularly useful for crusting or persistent dryness.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="NeilMed NasoGel Spray nasal moisturizer bottle" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="112px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity category="product" value="NeilMed NasoGel Spray"/>**

      A convenient moisturizing spray for use during the day. Follow the package directions.
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

A bedside cool-mist humidifier may also help, particularly if symptoms worsen overnight. Avoid medicated decongestant sprays unless otherwise indicated.

## Combined sicca symptom care plan

| Symptom | Supportive treatment |
|---|---|
| Dry eyes | **Tear Plus** lubricating eye drops as planned; confirm formulation with ophthalmology |
| Dry mouth | Sugar-free xylitol lozenges or XyliMelts |
| Dry nose | Ayr Saline Nasal Gel, 2–3 times daily as needed |

These provide symptomatic relief while the autoimmune and medication-related sicca evaluation proceeds.

**One additional clinical point:** Given that she is taking ophthalmic timolol, I would have ophthalmology review whether this is contributing to the ocular and oral dryness. Persistent nasal crusting, bleeding, or ulceration would also warrant nasal examination.

# TER RIV – ECW Clinic Output

## 1. Patient Contact and Care Information – TER RIV

**Patient:** TER RIV  
**DOB:** Not Provided  
**Provider:** Dr. Karandeep Singh  
**Date:** 11/23/2026  
**Pharmacy:** Walmart  
**Concern:** Dry eyes, dry mouth, and dry nose.

## 2. Front Desk Instructions – TER RIV

### A. Billing & CPT Codes
- **99214** – Established patient office visit only.
- No EKG or G2211.

### C. Medication Coordination
1. [ ] To Do – Coordinate discontinuation of ophthalmic timolol with ophthalmology and obtain a replacement if needed for eye-pressure control.
2. [ ] To Do – Provide instructions for Tears Plus, NeilMed NasoGel Spray, XyliMelts, and ACT Dry Mouth.

### D. Laboratory Orders
1. [ ] To Do – Order ANA with reflex, SSA/Ro, SSB/La, rheumatoid factor, ESR, CRP, CBC with differential, CMP, HbA1c, TSH, free T4, C3, C4, quantitative immunoglobulins, SPEP, and urinalysis.
2. [~] Pending Provider Clarification – Confirm ICD-10 linkage for sicca evaluation and laboratory destination.

### G. Scheduling
1. [ ] To Do – Keep the previously scheduled appointment unchanged.
2. [ ] To Do – Contact patient sooner if urgent or significant laboratory abnormalities require review.

## 3. Patient Instructions (English)

**Dry mouth:** Use XyliMelts sugar-free dry-mouth discs. If unavailable, use ACT Dry Mouth sugar-free lozenges, available at Walmart.

**Dry nose:** Use NeilMed NasoGel moisturizing nasal spray as directed.

**Dry eyes:** Continue Tears Plus lubricating drops. Dr. Singh recommends stopping timolol eye drops; coordinate the change with your eye doctor to ensure continued eye-pressure treatment.

**Blood tests:** Complete the ordered blood work to evaluate autoimmune conditions, including Sjögren disease, inflammation, thyroid function, diabetes, and other potential causes of dryness.

**Follow-up:** Keep your existing appointment. We will call sooner if urgent results require attention.

## 4. Patient Instructions (Spanish)

**Boca seca:** Use XyliMelts sin azúcar. Si no lo encuentra, puede comprar ACT Dry Mouth sin azúcar en Walmart.

**Nariz seca:** Use el aerosol hidratante nasal NeilMed NasoGel según las instrucciones.

**Ojos secos:** Continúe usando Tears Plus. El Dr. Singh recomienda suspender timolol; coordine el cambio con su oftalmólogo para mantener el control de la presión ocular.

**Análisis de sangre:** Complete los estudios solicitados para investigar enfermedades autoinmunes, incluyendo Sjögren, inflamación, tiroides, diabetes y otras causas de resequedad.

**Seguimiento:** Mantenga su cita previamente programada. Le llamaremos antes si algún resultado urgente requiere atención.

**FINAL-OK TO PRINT**
